links.note: The 'experiment' Camusfearna was thought suitable for - keeping an otter. 24198 is that West Highland cottage.
Camusfearna as the place for the otter experiment - the cottage Mij eventually lives in.
Camusfearna as the setting for the otter experiment - 24198's cottage.
The meaning of apathy - absence of interest. It glosses Mij's aloofness in the first twenty-four hours, before the attachment of 24202 formed.
Apathy as absence of interest - the state Mij begins in before becoming attached to the author.
In the beginning the otter was aloof and indifferent - the starting point of the attachment 24202 describes.
Mij aloof and indifferent at first - contrasted with the deep attachment he later forms.
What Mijbil did on the second night - came on to Maxwell's bed soon after midnight. The attachment forming.
What is wasted and provoking when left static - water. 24201 is Mij's love of water and his arranging its flow.
Water wasted and provoking when static - Mij's own principle about water.
Water must be kept on the move - Mij's love of water in 24201.
The meaning of 'an appalling spectacle' - a shocking scene, the phrase used of the box Mij had torn open before the flight.
'An appalling spectacle' as a shocking scene - the state of the travel box the airline insisted on.
What Mij did to the box - tore its lining. The box the airline required him to travel in.
Mij tearing the lining of the travel box - the consequence of the airline's rule.
What had trickled out of the box - blood, from Mij's struggle inside it. The airline's box in 24203.
Blood trickling from the box - what the airline's requirement did to Mij.
How Mij was to be transported to England - packed in a box, because the airline would not carry him in the cabin.
Mij to travel packed in a box - the airline restriction of 24203.
The meaning of 'compulsive habits' - habits impossible to control, used of Mij's fixed routines on the London walks.
'Compulsive habits' explained - the routines Mij kept on his London exercise route.
What kept Mij engaged in London - a ping-pong game he invented. 24200 is his inventing games and playing with great energy.
The ping-pong game that occupied Mij - the playfulness of 24200.
Where the Arabs kept the otter - in a sack. The moment Maxwell obtains Mij in Iraq.
The otter delivered in a sack - how Maxwell came by Mij.
Mij resembling a small dragon when first seen - Maxwell's first sight of the otter he had obtained.
The otter looking like a dragon at first sight - the acquisition scene in 24194.
The otter's dragon-like first appearance - when Maxwell first got him.
The dragon-like otter emerging from the sack - Maxwell's first sight of Mij.
The name given to the otter - Mijbil. 24195 is the naming.
Mijbil as the otter's name - 24195's subject.
When the author travelled - the New Year of 1956, the journey on which he got the otter.
The New Year of 1956 journey to Iraq, where Mij was obtained.
Why he goes to Basra and how long he waits - to collect his mail, and the otter arrives there. The acquisition of 24194.
The author travelled to Southern Iraq - the journey on which he acquired Mij.
Otters commonly found in the Tigris - what put the idea of an otter into the author's head.
The narrator and his friend going to Basra - the stage of the trip at which Mij was delivered.
The telephone exchange closed for a religious holiday - part of the delay in Basra before the otter arrived.
The otter's body covered in mud when first seen - Maxwell's first sight of the animal he had obtained.
It took a month to bring out his actual colour - the state Mij arrived in when Maxwell got him.
